1.explanation:
1. TableBatchActions.js – this component renders the batch actions bar and currently only shows the selected count and any child TableBatchAction buttons; it needs to accept new props (e.g. a selectAll callback, totalRowCount) and render the “Select all” control under the right conditions.
2. DataTable.tsx – defines the getBatchActionProps API and passes state/actions into TableBatchActions; it must be updated to supply the selectAll action and total row count so that the new button can invoke cross-page selection.
3. DataTable-batch-actions.stories.js – the Storybook example for batch actions; it should be extended to demonstrate the new “Select all” feature and document how to enable it.
4. TableBatchActions-test.js – unit tests for the batch actions bar; they need to be updated (or added) to assert that the new button appears when expected and that clicking it calls the selectAll handler.
5. DataTable.mdx – the usage documentation for DataTable and its batch actions; it should be updated to describe the new prop(s) and show example markup for including the “Select all” button in the toolbar.
1.bug_scenario: The request is to enhance the DataTable’s batch actions toolbar by adding an optional “Select all” control next to the “x items selected” summary. Currently TableBatchActions only lets you select rows on the current page via the TableSelectAll checkbox, but it doesn’t offer a built-in UI to select every row across all pages. The screenshots illustrate how Gmail surfaces a “Select all N conversations” link alongside the per‐page summary, and the design prototype shows a “Select all (1228)” button next to “50 items selected.”

2.explanation:
• DataTable.tsx – this is where getBatchActionProps and the selectAll action are defined; we need to extend its API to know when to show a built-in select-all button and wire it to the selectAll() action.
• TableBatchActions.js – this component renders the batch action bar and currently only renders its children; it must be updated to accept a new prop (e.g. showSelectAll or selectAllButtonText) and render the button next to the totalSelected text.
• __tests__/TableBatchActions-test.js – tests for TableBatchActions must be updated (or added) to verify the button shows and that clicking it calls the right handler.
• stories/DataTable-batch-actions.stories.js – the Storybook example for batch actions needs a new variant demonstrating the built-in select-all button and documenting the new prop.
• DataTable.mdx – the MDX usage docs for DataTable should include the new optional prop and usage guidance for the select-all button, so consumers know how to enable it.
2.bug_scenario: When users engage batch actions in a DataTable (for example, selecting 50 rows on page 1 of many), they sometimes need to “Select all” rows across every page (e.g. all 1,228 or 24,521 items). The current TableBatchActions component only shows the number of items selected on the current page and does not render a built-in “Select all across pages” control next to that count. The feature request is to make it easy to opt into a “Select all (totalCount)” button inside of the TableBatchActions bar, same as Gmail’s “Select all conversations” link.
